description.value: The study examined whether anodal transcranial direct current stimulation over the left inferior frontal gyrus, paired with language therapy, altered resting-state functional connectivity and whether connectivity changes were associated with improvements in written naming in people with primary progressive aphasia.

design.value: Participants belonged to a larger cohort receiving tDCS and sham plus language therapy in a double-blinded, within-subject crossover design. The present analysis used only the first stimulation phase and therefore a between-subject comparison of participants initially assigned to tDCS versus sham.

description.value: Participants initially assigned to anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus paired with speech-language therapy.

clinical_characteristics.value: All had a history of at least two years of progressive language deficits with no other etiology, atrophy predominantly in the left hemisphere and no primary memory deficits. The tDCS group included 5 participants with lvPPA, 3 with nfvPPA, and 4 with svPPA.

description.value: Participants initially assigned to a sham stimulation procedure paired with speech-language therapy.

clinical_characteristics.value: All had a history of at least two years of progressive language deficits with no other etiology, atrophy predominantly in the left hemisphere and no primary memory deficits. The sham group included 3 participants with lvPPA, 5 with nfvPPA, and 4 with svPPA.

task_description.value: Each condition consisted of daily therapy sessions in which patients received either tDCS or sham simultaneous with the start of language therapy. The language therapy involved oral and written picture naming/spelling therapy and used a spell-study-spell procedure.

design_type.value: between-subject first-phase analysis within a larger double-blinded, within-subject crossover design

instructions.value: The patient was shown a picture on the computer, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down. If the patient could not name the object, he was asked to talk about the picture and provide three properties of the pictured item.

stimuli.value: Pictures representing 10–30 trained words selected according to the level of language severity; matched untrained words were also evaluated.

task_performance_measures.value: percentage of correct letters in trained words

task_description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were collected before treatment, immediately after the treatment phase, and two months post-intervention to examine changes in functional connectivity.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were acquired for approximately 9 min before, after, and two months post-intervention.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Structural scans were acquired axially with a scan time of 6 min and 150 slices.

Anodal stimulation was delivered over the left inferior frontal gyrus at 2 mA for a maximum of 20 min in the tDCS condition and 30 s in the sham condition. The center of stimulation corresponded to the F7 electrode; electrode patches were 5 × 5 = 25 cm2, and the cathode was placed on the participant's right cheek.

description.value: MPRAGE scans were processed in MRICloud using an atlas-based analysis approach. High-resolution MPRAGE images were segmented with a multi-atlas fusion label algorithm and large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping; parcels were co-registered to resting-state dynamics and analyses were performed in native space. ROI volumes were normalized by total intracerebral volume.

Co-registration of structural scans with resting-state fMRI into the same anatomical space
Motion and intensity TR outlier rejection using ART, with thresholds of 2 standard deviations for motion and 4 standard deviations for intensity
Regression of the movement matrix and physiological nuisance matrix in a deconvolution regression for remaining TRs
Extraction of time courses from 19 cortical and deep gray matter ROIs
Calculation of Pearson correlations and Fisher z-transformed scores

model_type.value: semi-parametric method for average treatment effect estimation

model_settings.value: For each pair of ROIs, baseline z-transformed correlations, age, sex, years post-onset, PPA variant, language severity, total severity, and left IFG volume were considered as covariates. Forward model selection using Akaike information criterion was performed separately for tDCS and sham groups before combining them to estimate the average treatment effect. Standard sandwich estimator with adjustment for small sample size was used for standard errors, and Wald statistics were used for hypothesis testing. P-values were adjusted for family-wise error rate using the Holm procedure.

estimator.value: automated covariate selection; Akaike information criterion; standard sandwich estimator; asymptotic two-sided Wald tests

model_settings.value: Tests were conducted on the difference in absolute change in percentage correct from before and after treatment for tDCS versus sham groups.
One sample t-tests were used to test pre-post changes within treatment groups.

For each ROI pair with an unadjusted P-value < .05 in the treatment effect analysis, the before-and-after behavioral difference was regressed against the before-and-after functional connectivity correlation difference. t-tests were performed on model coefficients.

estimator.value: ordinary linear regression with t-tests on model coefficients
